events.name: The Science - and Art - of Regenerative Economics: Revolutionary Thinking for a World in Crisis
events.description_md:
# **The Science and Art of Regenerative Economics: Revolutionary Thinking for a World in Crisis**

Join us for a Monday morning conversation with John Fullerton about his new book and what an economy built on the logic of living systems would look like. John will share where his thinking has gone since the book came out, then open the floor.

The argument has two halves that rarely get discussed together. One is rigorous science, drawn from how living systems actually work. The other is art, because applying any of it in a particular place, and shifting how people see the economy in the first place, is a work of imagination.

## **The science**

Regenerative economics rests on a deceptively simple idea. An economic system should follow the same patterns that govern every other living system we know of. Those patterns are not metaphors. They have been studied for decades across ecology, network science and thermodynamics, and they hold whether you are looking at a forest, a watershed, a body or an economy.

The framework moves past sustainability, circularity and degrowth to diagnose the root cause of the polycrisis, the compounding effects of climate chaos, biodiversity loss and widening inequality. It points toward abundance rather than austerity, and toward a set of design principles rather than another round of crisis management.

More on the book: [https://capitalinstitute.org/regenerative-economics-book/](https://capitalinstitute.org/regenerative-economics-book/)

## **The art**

Knowing the principles tells you almost nothing about how to apply them in a particular place, with particular people and a particular history. That work is design, judgment and imagination, and it cannot be optimized.

The larger shift, where enough people stop seeing the economy as a machine and start seeing it as a living system they belong to, will move through culture as much as through economics. So John wants to put a question to the room. Most of the strongest work being made about this crisis says, correctly, that we are in serious trouble. That is true and incomplete. How do you tell the whole truth about where we are without foreclosing the way through, and what could artists make of that problem?

## **About John Fullerton**

John Fullerton is an unconventional economist, author, and impact investor widely considered the architect of Regenerative Economics. He is the founder of Capital Institute, dedicated to the bold reimagination of economics and finance aligned with and in service to life.

After a successful 20-year career on Wall Street where he was a Managing Director of what he calls "the old JPMorgan," John listened to a persistent inner voice and walked away in 2001 with no plan but many questions. Those questions became his life's work.

His 2025 book, _[Regenerative Economics: Revolutionary Thinking for a World in Crisis](https://capitalinstitute.org/regenerative-economics-book/)_ (New Society Publishers), is the culmination of that inquiry. He is a member of the Club of Rome, and he and James Lovelock were featured in the 2021 award-winning documentary _Going Circular_.

## **Practical**

Books will be available for sale and John will sign.

events.name: We Already Have the Solutions. So Why Aren't We Using Them? Live Podcast with Dr. Ayana Elizabeth Johnson
events.description_md:
Marine biologist Dr. Ayana Elizabeth Johnson has a take: we already have the climate solutions we need, we just need to actually implement them. If the tools exist and we're still not using them, then the thing standing in the way isn't technology or knowledge – it's us, and the arrangements we've agreed to live inside.

Michael Mezzatesta brings the Better Future podcast to NY Climate Week to put this take to the test. Expect an intimate conversation on what's still unsolved, who's refusing to build a better future, and what we can actually do about it.

PLEASE NOTE: Podcast recording begins at 4:00pm ET sharp - doors close at this time.

events.name: Our Crises Call for Re-enchantment: a Panel and Portal
events.description_md:
Join us in an equinox invitation to shift the groundswell of our minds towards possibilities that help us meet this moment.

Exploring re-enchantment as an approach to the metacrisis, from play to time to the unseen, we’ll embark on an ontological adventure for this world between worlds.

Part academic panel, part story circle, and part portal, an indoor discussion will spill outside into a gentle nature ritual to embrace the equinox, when our day is as long as our night, and we turn towards the darkness of our unknowing.

In conversation with:

**Jeremy D Johnson** -- Jeremy Johnson is a Mexican-American writer, speaker, and philosopher whose work ‘thinks with the root,’ investigating the deep-running transformations of culture and consciousness and their necessary role in opening ecological futures. He is the founder of the Mutations Network, a para-academic learning community and occasional podcast, and the author of _[Seeing Through the World: Jean Gebser and Integral Consciousness](https://amzn.to/2PXZN0K)_ (2019). His forthcoming book, _Fragments of an Integral Future: Essays on Time, Ecology, and a New Worldview,_ will be published this year.

[https://jeremydjohnson.substack.com/](https://jeremydjohnson.substack.com/)

**Sophia Rokhlin** \-- Sophia Rokhlin is a writer, speaker, and development advisor supporting the conservation of traditional ecological knowledge and land rights. She stewards community with [Ma Earth](https://maearth.com/), an organization building tools to collectively fund community-led regeneration. She is co-author of _[When Plants Dream: Ayahuasca, Amazonian Shamanism and the Psychedelic Renaissance](https://uk.bookshop.org/p/books/when-plants-dream-ayahuasca-amazonian-shamanism-and-the-global-psychedelic-renaissance-daniel-pinchbeck/d5804d30c6fd1490?ean=9781786785459)_ [](https://uk.bookshop.org/p/books/when-plants-dream-ayahuasca-amazonian-shamanism-and-the-global-psychedelic-renaissance-daniel-pinchbeck/d5804d30c6fd1490?ean=9781786785459)(2019), and previously worked with Amazonian land rights organizations including Rainforest Foundation US and Chaikuni Institute. Her research and writing has been featured in publications including The New York Times, PBS, and the BBC.

[https://www.sophiarokhlin.com/](https://www.sophiarokhlin.com/)

**Henry Kramer** -- Born and raised in the Hudson Valley, Henry Kramer’s interdisciplinary scholarship centers on the role of wonder and imagination in our relationship with the more-than-human world. Through writing, teaching, community building, music, storytelling, and experience design, Henry is animated by the project of depthful and playful re-enchantment. Henry currently teaches religion at Hunter College (CUNY) and serves as Academic Dean of the [Strother School of Radical Attention](https://www.schoolofattention.org/).

[https://www.instagram.com/henry.r.kramer/](https://www.instagram.com/henry.r.kramer/)

**Sadie Rittman** -- Sadie Rittman is a cultural ecologist exploring hidden worlds and re-enchantment in the context of the metacrisis. A creative scholar trained in anthropology, her work appears in _Orion Magazine, Perspectiva, Resilience, Edge Effects, The Journal for the Study of Religion, Nature and Culture,_ and elsewhere. She publishes _A Wider World_ on Substack, and is the founder of [Fairy Tale Lab](https://www.fairy-tale-lab.com/), a project to reclaim, heal, and hold what we’ve learned not to see. Born in New York and raised in Singapore, she’s lived between several worlds.

[sadierittman.substack.com](https://sadierittman.substack.com)

events.name: TrashBlitz with 5 Gyres [Field Trip]
events.description_md:
TrashBlitz is a data collection platform that empowers community-focused research by making it easy to collect data on brands, materials, and items found in the environment. Through the platform, community members can build datasets of plastic pollution impacting the local region and ecosystem. The data collected informs policy solutions, supports education, and demonstrates the need for relevant action plans.

5 Gyres will debut a new feature in the app, Photocapture, at Climate Week NYC. This tool allows users to snap a photo of trash on a walk, hike, or during a cleanup and instantly log it into our global database, further supporting solutions to plastic pollution.

Tuesday, Sept 22nd: Join us as we talk trash, TrashBlitz from 5 to 7 PM in the East Village at Tompkins Square Park, and grab a cocktail after at Caravan of Dreams!

Questions? Email [nick@5gyres.org](mailto:nick@5gyres.org) or text (908) 566 6137.

events.name: What to Do as the World Falls Apart With Nate Hagens - Metacrisis Salon #15
events.description_md:
[**Nate Hagens**](https://www.thegreatsimplification.com/) has spent twenty years studying and breaking down the more-than-human predicament we find ourselves in. Energy, money, ecology, and human behavior are not separate crises. Climate disruption, rising inequality, and weakening democratic institutions, amidst a sea of disconnection, are all outputs of the same machine that offers virtually no solutions.

This is why we find ourselves in a predicament and not a problem. Problems have solutions. Predicaments have responses.

This salon will focus on what good responses looks like.

If you’ve been struggling to retain a feeling of agency in a time of chaos - this talk is for you.

You'll leave seeing more clearly, with a map for navigating, and a few more people to walk into it alongside.

**Every salon we host sells out. Don't wait to get a ticket.**

events.name: Aligning AI Safety with Earth: Salon
events.description_md:
AI’s energy use is well discussed, yet the values AI models themselves prioritize could be vastly consequential on climate and nature—especially as AI systems become increasingly powerful and agentically autonomous.

This intimate salon will bring together a brain trust to explore how to ensure stewardship of Earth systems can become an explicit consideration in AI foundation model safety, training, evaluation, governance, and alignment research.

Following from work via the Earth Alignment Project and the National Academy of Sciences, we invite leaders from across businesses, philanthropy, civil society to consider: How should increasingly capable AI systems account for the long-term stewardship of the Earth systems that underpin human thriving? How might we get stewardship prioritized in the mainstream AI Safety and Alignment agenda and movement?

Capacity for this session is limited to ensure targeted conversation in our 90-minute window. No panel, this is a collective conversation and working group to set forth the opportunity and have participants input into prioritized values and approaches for aligning AI. Light food and beverage refreshments will be served.

The Earth Alignment Project's mission is to advance AI model alignment to safeguard the systems that sustain life.

events.name: Krill Baby Krill: Piloting an Activist Investment Trust for the Antarctic
events.description_md:
What if an environmental campaign could simultaneously shrink the market for an extractive industry and accelerate investment in its alternatives?

Krill sits at the foundation of the Antarctic food web, **but this critical ecosystem is being pushed beyond its limits.**

Industrial vessels are harvesting krill at record scale. Competing with whales, penguins and seals for their essential food source, this industry is siphoning the foundation of the Antarctic ecosystem into non-essential commercial products like omega-3 supplements—even as viable krill-free alternatives exist.

Overstories and Collective Capital Lab are developing a new campaign model designed to challenge the social and commercial license of this extractive industry while helping accelerate the market for its alternatives.

At its core: an Activist Investment Trust focused on the Antarctic krill issue: pairing an independent campaign against industrial fishing with aligned investment in krill-free replacement technologies.

This is an invitation to a participatory working session to cross-pollinate expertise, pressure-test an emerging idea and help shape a new approach to moving capital against extraction and towards regeneration.

events.name: Biodiversity Love And Law: How Stories, Art, And Law Come Together For Biodiversity Protection
events.description_md:
**A conversation, strategy session, and live humpback whale Artivism experience.**

With the harm clause stripped from the Endangered Species Act (ESA) and our oceans and national parks opened to mining and drilling, it feels like a bleak moment for biodiversity in the United States.

So we're going straight to the people doing something about it, on both fronts this fight needs: the law, and the culture change that supports it.

**Earthjustice** is suing the Trump administration over the harm clause. We'll hear from the team on that case: what we should know, what happens next, and how we can help as storytellers, strategists, artivists, and movement builders.

**More Than Human Life** is fighting for the other half — the rights of nature — and it's the hopeful half. A river in New Zealand has legal personhood. So does a cloud forest in Ecuador. Enough people came to feel that a river was a someone rather than a something, and lawyers spent years turning that shift into language a court would accept.

**And on the culture side— culture shift supports policy shift.** Stories and art move people in ways arguments can't reach; law makes the shift real, enforceable, hard to undo. So we've asked Roxi Shohadaee of **Design Science Studio** — a regenerative incubator training artists and designers to shape what comes next — to bring the culture side to the table: how creative practice becomes a cultural movement. She’ll share activations she’s done all over the world, including renegade projections in front of biodiversity COP delegations’ windows, and many other wild stories. Along with insights from **Climate Shifted**, an award-nominated podcast about best practices in climate Artivism, psychology, and behavior design.

Together we'll chart the path ahead — how we support biodiversity, and each other, with the skills each of us brings.

**Plus, a live taste of the culture shift**: host Eva Frye will guide you through an Artivism experience she’s been using to end commercial whaling in Iceland- powerful recordings of humpback whales hunting in Gitga'at waters, using awe to help people fall in love with these creatures so they want to protect them.

## DETAILS

Thursday, September 24 · 4:00–6:00pm

Caravan of Dreams · 405 E 6th St, East Village, NYC

4:00–5:30 Whale acoustics + conversation

5:30–6:00 Mingle

## SPEAKERS

**César Rodríguez-Garavito** — Founding Director, More-Than-Human Life (MOTH) Program, NYU School of Law

MOTH advances legal recognition for rivers, forests, fungi, and whales — including a partnership with Project CETI on the legal implications of decoding sperm whale communication.

**Ben Levitan** — Senior Attorney, Earthjustice

Lead counsel on the ESA "harm" fight. Earthjustice is the nation's largest nonprofit environmental law organization, litigating on behalf of clients free of charge.

**Roxi Shohadaee** — Director + ARTchitect, Design Science Studio

Roxi builds programs that builds capacity for artists and designers to become regenerative-futures practitioners, and has created a multitude of activations for wildlife, like for the Campaign for Nature and the 30x30 Challenge, and Biodiversity COP in Montreal.

**Moderated by Eva Frye** — Host, Climate Shifted; whale artivist

Climate Shifted is an Ambies-nominated podcast about what actually works to move people on climate. Eva works with the emotion of awe to help people fall in love with whales — so they want to protect them.

events.name: True Human: A Story Big Enough to Carry Us
events.description_md:
We hover within an epochal threshold, a tempestuous passage from the Age of Separation to the Age of Homecoming. The stories that have scaffolded civilization are reaching the end of their fitness to carry us forward.

Movements hinge on stories. The Climate Movement cannot succeed unless we facilitate an ontological shift from the story of separation and dominion to the story of interdependence and homecoming.

Most people aren't even talking about this. But, it may be the most important conversation of our age.

[**True Human: Reimagining Ourselves at the End of Our World**](https://www.samanthasweetwater.com/truehuman) is a companion through the collapse of one world and the emergence of another — one rooted in biospiritual wisdom, sacred reciprocity, and embodied participation in Life.

Join me if you want to address the human conundrum at the level of cause, and if you're interested in aligning human systems and stories with flourishing life.

Come explore ways being, stories, concepts, and practices of True Human. Make the one shift that shifts everything: put Life at the center of all that you be, do and become. Gain vision, language, practices and strength to guide the your life and work.

Bring your copy of True Human. I'll be signing books after the talk.

**Samantha Sweetwater** is a Gaian philosopher, keynote speaker, transformational facilitator and coach for 30+ years, and author of True Human: Reimagining Ourselves at the End of Our World.

events.description_md:
There is a new way we can fight the climate crisis.

Join us in the Climate Engagement Lab to experience how we can ground our engagement efforts in core emotions.  Because ​facts are never enough to change what we do – as individuals, as a local community, as a nation, on the earth. They matter, but so do our core emotions and belief systems.

Come to Caravan of Dreams on Friday the 25th.

Or come on Wednesday the 23rd to the Rockefeller Boardroom: [https://www.climateweeknyc.org/event-search/the-climate-engagement-lab](https://www.climateweeknyc.org/event-search/the-climate-engagement-lab)

Participate at either location and learn how, by working together, we can rebalance the lopsided emphasis on facts and put human emotion at the center of a new climate narrative. Learn how we can map people’s emotions to climate and inspire people to insist on action and solutions.

You will be active participants in the demonstration of how we can design a narrative that engages people emotionally.

(Other than a darkened room and powerful visual presentations, there are no flashing lights or other stimuli.)

events.name: The More-Than-Human City
events.description_md:
Drop into a slow experience of the living world after a busy Climate Week. Can we commune with nature in one of the most chaotic parks in New York? Let's find out. (Yes.)

Join [Dear Crisis](https://dearcrisis.com/climateweek) and [Earthling](https://www.earthling.so/) for a field trip to look closely at what's blooming, buzzing, fruiting, foraging, and otherwise _alive_ in Tompkins Square Park and the community gardens of the East Village.

Through guided exploration and discussion, we'll practice identifying our nonhuman neighbors and ask: How does a plant keep time and why do some bloom so late in summer? Which creatures stick around all year, and who is passing through for the season? What does a pigeon sense that we don’t?

We'll embrace New York as a more-than-human city—one where New Yorkers, human and nonhuman, live in close connection and interdependence. Seeing the city through this lens not only opens up opportunities for daily wonder, but also sets the stage for climate resilience.

In other words: let's touch grass.

**WHERE AND WHEN**

We will depart from Caravan of Dreams at 4:30 and walk within a 10-minute radius of the restaurant.

**WHAT TO BRING**

No need to know the names of the plants, own binoculars, or identify as a "nature person.” Just bring your curiosity and some comfortable walking shoes.

**FIELD NOTEBOOKS**

Notebooks are not necessary but encouraged! You can buy an Earthling field notebook with your ticket to record your observations from the event and your future explorations. We'll also have some available for sale at the event.

![](https://images.lumacdn.com/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,dpr=2,anim=false,background=white,quality=75,width=800/uploads/5b/e11e562c-5ec0-47a2-870e-bc3e5c67a79b.png)

**ABOUT EARTHLING**

Earthling OS is a tool to connect with local nature and participate in climate solutions. [Download the app](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/earthling-os/id6769650512?utm_source=luma) to learn about nearby ecology and plug into solutions wherever you are.

We aim to keep our events accessible. If money is an issue, please apply for financial assistance from our [Community Fund](https://dearcrisis.com/support).

events.name: Dear Crisis, Sincerely… Grief
events.description_md:
Participants will take part in a collective ritual and workshop exploring grief, memory, and our relationship to a changing climate. Through guided storytelling and altar-making, we'll reflect on what we're mourning, what we want to preserve, and how ceremonies have always signaled transformation and the next part of grief: action.

Together, we'll create an altar that reveals what our grief tells us about what we value and want to protect. Each participant will leave with a personal intention etched into the altar and a collective action ignited by the ceremony.

Co-hosted by Kayla Palisoc and Viv Tran

We aim to keep our events accessible. If money is an issue, please apply for financial assistance from our [Community Fund](https://dearcrisis.com/support).

events.name: Love and Fear in a Warming World
events.description_md:
[![](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/5mz_OLpa9BM/hqdefault.jpg)](https://youtube.com/watch?v=5mz_OLpa9BM)

Watch the full film: [https://vimeo.com/1092852064](https://vimeo.com/1092852064)

How do we navigate the emotions that come with climate change - fear, hope, uncertainty? And how can these emotions spur personal and collective climate action? Love and Fear in a Warming World is a 90-minute participatory experience that uses creative expression to help people reconnect with their values, their sense of purpose, and a shared climate-conscious community.

Through free writing, poetry, storytelling and shared reflection, participants explore what they love, what they fear losing, and how those feelings might become meaningful action. No artistic experience is needed. Past participants - from members of the UK Parliament to NGO and business leaders, artists, educators and climate-concerned citizens across India, Europe and the US - have described leaving with less climate anxiety, more clarity, and a deeper sense of connection to the climate movement.

Co-created by Slam Out Loud and Climate Shift, the workshop will be facilitated in person by Jigyasa Labroo. Slam Out Loud has brought arts-based learning to 2.5 million children in India and recently completed an RCT with researchers from Harvard and the Max Planck Institute showing how the arts can move children from helplessness to climate agency.

In the Dream Room at Caravan of Dreams. Part of Where Climate Week Comes to Dream: [https://dearcrisis.com/climateweek](https://dearcrisis.com/climateweek)  
  
We aim to keep our events accessible. If money is an issue, please apply for financial assistance from our [Community Fund](https://dearcrisis.com/support).

events.name: A Ritual of Story, Sound & Climate
events.description_md:
We are living through a planetary crossing — and our bodies and hearts know it. Grief & Longing. Ancestral rememberings. Collective heartbreak. Courting mystery. Deep-time listening. Cultural repair & renewal. Mythopoetic attunement. Embodiment & song. And the many other things that make us human. Let’s take a necessary moment to drop in with reverence and wonder and some appropriate praise for the place that has been holding us and our dreams

Join Asheville-based astrologer and storyteller Frank Salzano (Medicine of the Starry Heavens), and Brooklyn-based musician Lila Bloom for an immersive afternoon weaving together song circles, poetic myth-telling, and deep-time story to help us feel our way through the climate moment. Rather than another problem-solving conversation, this is a ritual of attuning — grounded in the living ecologies of the New York City watershed, its marshlands, rising tides, and ancient memory.

We'll move through harmonizing and voice to drop into the body together, then journey through the cosmos and climate mythos that connects us to this place and bridges our ancestral starlore to the current meta-crisis. From the Starry River to the Hudson, we will conclude with some shared reflections and integration, offering our musings, blessings and care back to this home we hold so dear.

The afternoon will unfold in three movements:

Opening — song circle & harmonizing to arrive together

Journey — poetic storytelling through climate, cosmos & the NYC watershed

Integration — group shares, Q&A & collective reflection and care

📍 Dream Room | 3:00–6:00 PM ET

In the Dream Room at Caravan of Dreams. Part of Where Climate Week Comes to Dream: [https://dearcrisis.com/climateweek](https://dearcrisis.com/climateweek)

events.name: Apocamate: Find Your Person/People Before the End of the World
events.description_md:
## Climate anxiety is more fun with company.

Join us for an evening of dark comedy, playful prompts, structured mingling, and low-stakes existential connection. Come looking for a date, a friend, a future collaborator, or simply someone who shares your preferred zombie-escape plan.

Expect a drink, an apocalypse-themed bingo card, fast conversation rounds, audience games, and a little climate comedy to keep the dread manageable.

This is not your average Brooklyn dating event. No forced intimacy, no endless awkward small talk—just funny people, good questions, and a room full of people trying to find their apocamate.  
  
\--

*   **Arrival & Liquid Courage** (30 min) — Grab a drink, break the ice, and pick up your survival badges.
*   **The Opening Salvo** (15 min) — Welcome, ground rules, and climate comedy to ease the existential dread.
*   **Survival Games & The Hot Seat** (30 min) — Interactive room exercises and rapid-fire audience moments.
*   **The Apocamate Rounds** (40 min) — Fast-paced, prompt-driven conversation rounds to find your co-pilot.
*   **After-Hours & The Date Me Wall** (30 min) — Final connections, late-night hang, and swapping coordinates.
